Register

In 1677, English Particular Baptists published what would become known as the Second London Baptist Confession of Faith, setting forth with remarkable clarity their understanding of the great doctrines of Scripture. Twelve years later, in 1689, Baptist churches were able to publicly own and affirm that confession together.

In 2027, 350 years after its first publication, pastors will gather for The Faith We Confess: 350 Years of the Second London Baptist Confession of Faith. This conference is not simply an opportunity to commemorate an important moment in Baptist history. It is an opportunity to consider again the biblical truths these men confessed and to ask what it means for pastors and churches to believe, preach, defend, and live those same truths faithfully in our own generation.

Over the course of five days, we will work through all 32 chapters of the Confession—from the Holy Scriptures and the doctrine of God to covenant, Christ, justification, sanctification, worship, marriage, the church, the ordinances, resurrection, and final judgment. The aim will be distinctly pastoral. These doctrines were never intended merely for the classroom or the theologian’s study. They shape the pulpit, the worship of the church, the shepherding of souls, the ordering of families, the training of the next generation, and the church’s faithfulness in the world.

Men will open the Scriptures and consider the continuing importance of this historic confession for the life and ministry of the church.

Church and Family Life, together with Covenant Baptist Theological Seminary, Christ the King Church, and Grace Bible Theological Seminary, is bringing pastors together for a week of preaching, fellowship, prayer, and serious theological reflection. Our desire is not merely that men leave knowing the 1689 better, but that they know the Scriptures better, love Christ more deeply, preach the whole counsel of God more clearly, and return to their churches strengthened for the work God has given them.

Three hundred and fifty years have passed since these truths were first put into print, but the Word of God has not changed. By God’s grace, we are still confessing the faith once for all delivered to the saints.

Speakers

Sam Waldron

Sam Waldron was a pastor of the Reformed Baptist Church of Grand Rapids from 1977-2001 and taught at Trinity Ministerial Academy from 1981 to 1989. Leaving there in 2001, he pursued a PhD at Southern Seminary in Louisville, KY. Having served as a pastor of Heritage Baptist Church in Owensboro, Kentucky from 2005-2013, he then became one of the pastors of Grace Reformed Baptist Church of Owensboro, Kentucky. He also serves as President and Professor of Systematic Theology of Covenant Baptist Theological Seminary.

Sam has been married to his dear wife Charlene since 1975. They have five children and at last count 15 grandchildren—all of whom they love very much. Sam enjoys reading, weight-lifting, walking, and spending time with his wife, children, and grandchildren.

Rob Ventura

Rob Ventura is one of the pastors of Grace Community Baptist Church of North Providence, Rhode Island. He is the author of Expository Outlines and Observations on Romans. He is a co-author of A Portrait of Paul, Spiritual Warfare and God is our Refuge and Strength, and is the general editor of Going Beyond the Five Points, Covenant Theology, and A New Exposition of The London Baptist Confession of Faith of 1689. He has also contributed articles to journals, periodicals and The Reformation Heritage KJV Study Bible. He and his wife, Vanessa, and family live in Rhode Island.

Scott Brown

Scott T. Brown is the president of Church and Family Life and pastor at Hope Baptist Church in Wake Forest, North Carolina. Scott graduated from California State University in Fullerton with a degree in History and received a Master of Divinity degree from Talbot School of Theology. He gives most of his time to local pastoral ministry, expository preaching, and conferences on church and family reformation. Scott helps people think through the two greatest institutions God has provided—the church and the family.

Brian Borgman

Brian Borgman is the founding pastor of Grace Community Church. He earned a BA in Biblical Studies from Biola University (La Mirada, CA), a Master of Divinity from Western Conservative Baptist Seminary (Portland, OR) and a Doctor of Ministry from Westminster Seminary (Escondido, CA) and a ThM from Puritan Reformed Theological Seminary in Historical Theology.

Brian and his wife Ariel have been married since 1987. They have three wonderful children, Ashley, Zach and Alex and three grandsons.

Justin Miller

Justin Miller is a husband, father, pastor, and, most importantly, a follower of the Lord Jesus. He holds a Doctor of Ministry from Whitefield Theological Seminary in Lakeland, FL, a Master of Theology from Union School of Theology in Bridgend, Wales (The Open University), a Master of Divinity from Liberty Baptist Theological Seminary in Lynchburg, and a Master of Accounting from Southern Illinois University at Carbondale. He is the Principal of Expositors Institute and is privileged to serve on the board of directors of Covenant Baptist Theological Seminary. He is Director of Savoring the Savior Books and is the author of several books, including: The Not So Loving Side of Gentle Parenting (2025), William Perkins on Pastoral Theology (2023), What is Faith? (2022), Unity with Rome? (2022), John Owen on Pastoral Preaching (2021), and Stop Worrying He Reigns (2018).

Michael Clary

Michael Clary is the founder and lead pastor of Christ the King Church in Fort Thomas, Kentucky and co-founder of King’s Domain ministries. Michael is the author of “God’s Good Design: A Biblical, Theological, and Practical Guide to Human Sexuality” (Reformation Zion, 2023) and a forthcoming book from Canon Press (early 2026).

Michael earned an M. Div. from the Southern Baptist Theological Seminary. He has published writings for American Reformer, The Blaze, Christ Over All, Center for Baptist Leadership, Clear Truth Media, The Federalist, Founders Ministry, King’s Domain, Sola Ecclesia, and Truth Script. He also publishes regularly on his own website at dmichaelclary.com.

Michael is the host of the Plain Speech Podcast and co-host of the Current Reality Podcast. He and his wife, Laura, live in Cincinnati with their four children.

Jeffrey D. Johnson

Jeffrey D. Johnson is a Pastor of Grace Bible Church, the President of Grace Bible Theological Seminary, and the founder of Free Grace Press. He graduated from Central Baptist College with a BS in Bible and earned his MRel in Biblical Studies and a DMin in Systematics from Veritas Theological Seminary. He is also the author of multiple books, including The Pursuit of Glory, The Church, and The Kingdom of God. He and his wife, Letha, live in Conway, Arkansas with their four children—Martyn, Christian, Britain, and Evelyn.

Robert Bosley

Robert Bosley is a member of Hope Baptist Church in Wake Forest, North Carolina. He and his wife, Andrea, have been married since 2012 and have seven children—five girls and two boys. He graduated from the College at Southeastern with a BA in Pastoral Ministry and is currently pursuing an MA in Biblical Studies at Covenant Baptist Theological Seminary. He also owns Dominion Woodworks, a custom cabinet and furniture workshop located in Youngsville, North Carolina.

Jon English Lee

Jon English Lee serves as the Academic Dean and a Professor of Systematic and Historical Theology at Covenant Baptist Theological Seminary. Previously he served as Pastor of Discipleship for Morningview Baptist Church in Montgomery, Alabama. He earned a Bachelor’s degree from Auburn University Montgomery, a Masters of Divinity from The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary, and a PhD in Systematic and Historical Theology from SBTS. He is a member of the Evangelical Theological Society and a Senior fellow for the Center for Pastor Theologians.

The venue

Christ the King Church

We are glad to gather at Christ the King Church, one of the conference’s host partners, pastored by speaker Michael Clary. The church exists “to help people know, love, and obey Jesus as Lord over all of life,” and gives itself to plain-spoken preaching from the Bible, prayer, household discipleship, and a multigenerational “oak tree” vision of ministry.

The church sits at the top of the hill in Fort Thomas, Kentucky, right off the highway—just across the Ohio River from downtown Cincinnati.

Frequently Asked Questions

When does the conference begin and end?

The conference begins on Monday, April 5, 2027, with registration opening at 12:00 PM and the first session beginning at 1:00 PM. The conference concludes on Friday, April 9, at 4:50 PM.

See the full daily schedule.

Where is the conference located?

The conference will be held at Christ the King Church, 638 Highland Avenue, Fort Thomas, KY 41075 (directions).

The church is located in the Greater Cincinnati area, just across the Ohio River from downtown Cincinnati.

What meals are included with registration?

Lunch will be provided Tuesday through Friday (four lunches total). Light refreshments and coffee will be available each morning, with coffee available throughout the day.

Dinner is not included, so attendees are free to explore the many restaurants in the surrounding Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky area.

Is this a family conference?

The conference is primarily designed for pastors and men interested in studying the Second London Baptist Confession of Faith. We especially encourage fathers to consider bringing their older children who would benefit from the teaching.

Who is this conference intended for?

The Faith We Confess is primarily a pastors’ conference, but it is open to anyone interested in studying the doctrines of the Second London Baptist Confession of Faith.

Whether you’re a pastor, elder, seminarian, or simply someone who desires a deeper understanding of these biblical truths, you’re welcome to join us.

Will the entire Second London Baptist Confession be covered?

Yes! Our goal is to work through all 32 chapters of the Second London Baptist Confession of Faith throughout the five-day conference.

Each session will examine the biblical doctrines expressed in the Confession, with a particular emphasis on their application to the life and ministry of the local church.

Can I register for just one or two days?

Registration covers the entire conference, and we do not offer discounted single-day or partial-conference registrations. You’re welcome to attend whichever days your schedule allows, but the registration fee remains the same regardless of how many days you attend.

Are there special registration rates for seminary students?

Yes! We offer a discounted registration rate of $249 for seminary students.

Are there discounts for groups attending from the same church?

We do not currently offer group discounts. Registration is priced individually, regardless of how many people attend from the same church.

Is there a registration deadline?

We encourage attendees to register as early as possible. Registration will remain open as space allows, but we recommend securing your spot early and making travel arrangements in advance.

What is the cancellation or refund policy?

We understand that plans sometimes change. Registrations may be canceled according to the following schedule:

  • On or before December 5, 2026: Full refund, less a 10% administrative processing fee.
  • December 6, 2026 – February 5, 2027: 50% refund.
  • After February 5, 2027: No refunds will be issued.

Registrations may also be transferred to another person through March 5, 2027. To request a transfer, please email info@cf.life with the updated attendee information.

Are there recommended hotels for the conference?

Yes! We’ve arranged discounted group rates at select hotels in the Greater Cincinnati area. Our recommended hotels and booking information are listed in the Lodging & Travel section above.

Most hotels in the surrounding Newport, Covington, and Cincinnati areas are approximately 10–15 minutes from the church.

We encourage you to book early, as discounted rooms are limited and available on a first-come, first-served basis.

What airport should I fly into?

We recommend flying into Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport (CVG).

CVG is approximately 15–20 miles from the conference location, depending on your route, and about a 20–30-minute drive from the church.

It’s also approximately 14–17 miles from the Hampton Inn & Suites Newport/Cincinnati, one of our recommended hotels.

Is transportation provided from the airport to the church or hotels?

We will not be providing an airport shuttle.

The easiest way to travel from Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport (CVG) to your hotel or the church is by Uber, Lyft, or rental car.

For a more economical option, the TANK 2X Airporter bus provides transportation from the airport to downtown Cincinnati for approximately $2 per person. From there, you can arrange an Uber or Lyft to your hotel or the church.

We also recommend checking with your hotel about available airport transportation.

Will I need a rental car during the conference?

A rental car is recommended but not required.

The church is approximately 10–15 minutes from many of the hotels in the area. If you’re flying in without a rental car, Uber and Lyft are available throughout the Greater Cincinnati area.

You may also wish to coordinate rides with other attendees staying at the same hotel.

Will parking be available at the church?

Yes! Free parking is available at Christ the King Church for all conference attendees.

Will there be books and resources available for purchase?

Yes! We plan to have a selection of books and theological resources available during the conference, including materials from participating ministries and publishers.

Will conference sessions be recorded?

Yes! All conference sessions will be recorded, and recordings will be provided to registered attendees following the event. Please allow a few months after the conference for the recordings to be processed and distributed.

Will seminary credit be available for attending?

If you’re interested in receiving seminary credit for attending the conference, we encourage you to contact your seminary directly to inquire about eligibility and any additional requirements.

Are there restaurants near the church?

Yes! There are plenty of great dining options in Fort Thomas, Newport, and the surrounding Cincinnati area, including inexpensive restaurants, casual dining, and upscale options. Here are a few recommendations:

Budget-Friendly$10–20 per person
  • Highland Square Deli – Sandwiches, wraps, soups, and salads, located right next to the church.
  • Mad Mike’s Burgers & Fries – Casual burgers and hand-cut fries in Newport.
Casual Dining$15–30 per person
  • Padrino Fort Thomas – A popular local Italian restaurant serving pizza, pasta, and sandwiches.
  • Midway Cafe – A neighborhood favorite known for its burgers and wings.
Upscale Dining$30–60+ per person
  • Otto’s – A well-regarded American bistro in Covington, serving Southern-inspired dishes.
  • Bouquet Restaurant – An upscale, farm-to-table restaurant in Covington offering seasonal dishes.

Most of these restaurants are a short drive from the church. We recommend checking hours and making reservations when appropriate.
